meta.title: Safety Toolkit | Shakti Shield
meta.description: Practical Do's and Don'ts for travel, night commute, online safety, workplace, and home, plus a personalised safety checklist generator.

toolkit.heroSubtitle: Practical Do's and Don'ts by situation, plus a personalised checklist you can use right away.

dos: Share your live trip details or vehicle number with a trusted contact before starting.
Check that cab or auto registration numbers match the booking app before boarding.
Keep your phone charged above 50% and carry a small power bank when possible.
Sit near other families, women passengers, or the exit in buses and trains.
donts: Do not share your home address or travel routine with strangers.
Do not accept open drinks or food from unknown co-passengers.
Do not board unverified or unmarked vehicles in isolated areas.
Do not wear both earphones at high volume; stay aware of your surroundings.

dos: Prefer well-lit main roads and busy stops even if the route takes a few extra minutes.
Keep 112 and a trusted family member on speed dial before stepping out.
Hold your phone and bag securely so your hands stay free to move quickly.
Ask a trusted friend or family member to stay on call during the last stretch home.
donts: Do not take unlit shortcuts through alleys, parks, or empty parking lots.
Do not wait outside alone if a cab is delayed; wait inside a lit shop or lobby.
Do not share live location publicly on social media while commuting at night.
Do not hesitate to enter a bright store, metro station, or police booth if someone follows you.

dos: Use strong, unique passwords and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on all accounts.
Set social media profiles and contact lists to private and review tagged photos.
Take screenshots with visible URLs, dates, and usernames if someone harasses you.
Report cyber harassment or financial fraud on cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930 (verify).
donts: Do not share OTPs, bank PINs, private photos, or identity documents with unknown contacts.
Do not click shortened or suspicious links promising prizes, jobs, or urgent account checks.
Do not delete abusive messages before saving screenshots or evidence.
Do not pay blackmail or sextortion demands; block, save evidence, and report immediately.

dos: Learn your organisation's Internal Committee (IC) process under the POSH Act 2013 (verify).
Save dates, times, messages, and witness names if uncomfortable behaviour happens.
Set clear communication boundaries for work hours and official channels.
Check whether complaints can also be submitted via the SHe-Box portal (verify).
donts: Do not ignore repeated inappropriate remarks or unwanted physical contact.
Do not meet alone in isolated rooms after hours if you feel uncomfortable.
Do not feel pressured to delete work chats or emails that show harassment.
Do not blame yourself; workplace safety is a legal duty of the employer.

dos: Keep doors, window latches, and peepholes in good working order.
Verify delivery or repair visitors through an intercom, window, or booking app before opening.
Keep emergency numbers (112, 181, 1091) and key documents easy to reach.
Agree on a simple code word with trusted neighbours or family for quiet help.
donts: Do not open the main door to unverified callers claiming urgent utility checks.
Do not leave spare keys in obvious places like under mats or flower pots.
Do not post photos showing you are alone at home or away on holiday in real time.
Do not ignore threats or abuse inside the home; reach out to 181 or 7827170170 (verify).

generator.heading: Personalised Safety Checklist
generator.subtitle: Pick your routine below to build a custom checklist. Nothing is uploaded or tracked.
generator.emptyPrompt: Select at least one situation above to generate your personalised checklist.

core: Save emergency number 112 and women helpline 181 in phone favourites.
Keep one trusted contact informed about your daily return time.
student: Save campus security, hostel warden, and local police station numbers.
Walk in pairs or groups when leaving evening classes or libraries.
Keep social media profiles private and avoid sharing live hostel check-ins.
working: Note your workplace Internal Committee (IC) contact under POSH Act 2013 (verify).
Use official company transport or share cab details when working late.
Keep personal phone numbers separate from public work directories where possible.
nightCommute: Charge your phone and carry a power bank before leaving work or college.
Check the vehicle number plate and driver details before getting in.
Stay on well-lit main roads and keep a trusted contact on call if uneasy.
soloTravel: Keep digital and paper copies of ID, ticket, and hotel address safely.
Verify hotel room locks and avoid announcing your room number aloud.
Share your daily itinerary and check-in times with family.
livingAlone: Use a peephole or door chain before opening to any delivery or visitor.
Keep a whistle or torch near your bedside and know your nearest exit.
Build a trusted contact check-in routine with a neighbour or relative.

meta.title: Incident Guide | Shakti Shield
meta.description: Calm, step-by-step guidance for stalking, online harassment, workplace issues, and domestic violence, including evidence tips, Zero FIR, and verified helplines.

incidentGuide.heroSubtitle: Calm, practical steps on what to do, what evidence to save, and where to report.
incidentGuide.safetyNoteBody: Pages you visit may remain visible in your browser history on shared devices. Use private or incognito browsing when needed, and use Quick Exit (or press Escape twice) anytime.
incidentGuide.wizardSubtitle: Select a situation below to see tailored steps, evidence to keep, reporting options, and verified helplines.

stalking.lawRef: Relevant law: BNS Section 78 (verify from official sources).
steps: Move immediately to a bright, populated public place, store, or security desk.
Call 112 or alert a trusted family member or friend with your location.
Vary your daily commute route and timings if someone follows you repeatedly.
evidence: Write down dates, times, places, and any vehicle number or physical description.
Save threatening texts, missed call logs, voicemails, or social media messages.
Note names of witnesses or nearby shops with CCTV cameras so footage can be requested quickly.
report: Call 112 in immediate danger or 1091 / 181 for women's support (verify state availability).
File a complaint or Zero FIR at any police station under BNSS Section 173 (relevant law: BNS Section 78; verify).

steps: Do not reply to threats or pay blackmail demands; block or mute the sender after saving proof.
Change passwords and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on email and social accounts.
Tell a trusted person or counsellor so you do not have to handle it alone.
evidence: Take full screenshots showing profile URLs, usernames, dates, and exact messages.
Save transaction IDs, UPI details, or bank statements if financial fraud occurred.
Keep original files or emails without cropping or editing metadata.
report: Report online at cybercrime.gov.in or call cyber fraud helpline 1930 (verify).
You can also file an FIR or e-FIR / Zero FIR at a police station under BNSS Section 173.

workplace.lawRef: Relevant law: POSH Act 2013 (complaints can also go through the SHe-Box portal; verify).
steps: Prioritise your safety: step away from isolated spaces and inform a trusted colleague or friend.
Check your workplace policy for the Internal Committee (IC) contact details.
Write down a clear timeline of what happened while details are fresh.
evidence: Save work emails, chat messages, meeting invites, and call logs safely on a personal device.
Record dates, times, locations, exact words used, and names of any witnesses.
Keep copies of any formal complaints and acknowledgement receipts.
report: Submit a written complaint to your organisation's Internal Committee (IC) under POSH Act 2013 (verify).
Complaints can also go through the SHe-Box portal (verify), or to police via BNSS Section 173 if a criminal offence occurred.

domestic.lawRef: Relevant law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 (verify).
steps: If you are in immediate physical danger, leave to a safe room or neighbour's home and call 112.
Keep emergency cash, ID proofs, phone charger, and key medical papers accessible if safe.
Reach out to a trusted family member, friend, or women helpline 181 / 7827170170 (verify).
evidence: Save photos of injuries or damaged property with dates, and keep hospital or doctor records.
Keep abusive messages, threat recordings, or financial control records safely.
Note dates of incidents and names of neighbours, relatives, or doctors who witnessed harm.
report: Call 112 for urgent police help, 181 (24x7 women helpline), or NCW domestic violence helpline 7827170170 (verify).
Seek help under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 (verify) or file an FIR under BNSS Section 173.

fir.heading: Understanding Zero FIR, Free Copy & Police Refusal
fir.subtitle: Your basic rights when reporting a crime under BNSS (verify from official sources).
fir.zeroFirBody: A Zero FIR can be registered at any police station regardless of where the offence happened, and the police must give you a copy of the FIR free of cost.
fir.refusalTitle: If Police Refuse to Register an FIR
fir.refusalStep1: 1. Write directly to the Superintendent of Police explaining the incident and the refusal.
fir.refusalStep2: 2. If action is still not taken, approach the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3).

meta.title: Cyber Safety Centre | Shakti Shield
meta.description: Supportive guidance on sextortion, fake profiles, deepfakes, privacy settings, and reporting via cybercrime.gov.in and helpline 1930 (verify).

cyber.heroSubtitle: Clear steps for online threats, privacy protection, and official reporting.
cyber.supportBanner: If someone threatens, impersonates, or blackmails you online, it is not your fault. Save evidence and seek help right away.
cyber.threatsHeading: Common Online Threats & What to Do
cyber.threatsSubtitle: Calm, practical actions you can take immediately.

sextortion.title: Sextortion & Blackmail
sextortion.summary: Someone threatens to share private photos, videos, or messages unless you pay or comply.
steps: Do not pay money or send more images; paying rarely stops demands.
Take clear screenshots of messages, profiles, URLs, and payment requests before blocking.
Report immediately on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 for financial demands (verify), and tell a trusted person.

fakeProfiles.title: Fake Profiles & Impersonation
fakeProfiles.summary: Someone creates an account using your name, photos, or phone number without permission.
steps: Capture the full profile URL, handle, and screenshots of misused photos or posts.
Use the platform's 'Report Impersonation' tool and ask trusted friends to report the account too.
Inform close contacts not to respond to the fake account and report on cybercrime.gov.in (verify).

deepfakes.title: Deepfakes & Edited Media
deepfakes.summary: Someone alters your photos, voice, or video using editing or AI tools without consent.
steps: Save the link, platform name, account details, and screenshots showing where the media appears.
Request urgent takedown through the platform's non-consensual imagery or harassment form.
File a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in (verify) or at a police station via BNSS Section 173.

privacy.heading: Privacy Settings Checkup
privacy.subtitle: Tick each setting as you review your phone and social accounts (stays only on this page).
items: Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) using an authenticator app or secure code on email and social accounts.
Set social profiles to Private, limit who can message or tag you, and hide your phone number and friend list.
Turn off automatic location tagging in your camera and social media posts.
Review app permissions (camera, microphone, contacts, location) and remove access for unused apps.
Use unique, strong passwords for banking, email, and social media accounts.

reporting.heading: How & Where to Report Cyber Incidents
reporting.subtitle: Use official portals and helplines; always verify current state procedures from official sources.
reporting.portalBody: Report online harassment, sextortion, fake profiles, and deepfake abuse at cybercrime.gov.in (verify from official sources).
reporting.helplineBody: If money is involved or at risk, call 1930 as soon as possible (availability can vary by state; verify from official sources). In immediate physical danger, call 112.
steps: 1. Save uncropped screenshots showing full URLs, usernames, dates, and times.
2. Note bank transaction IDs or UPI references if any payment or fraud occurred.
3. Submit your report on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 (verify) and save the complaint acknowledgement number.
4. You may also approach any police station to file an FIR / Zero FIR under BNSS Section 173.

meta.title: Know Your Rights | Shakti Shield
meta.description: Searchable and filterable guide to women's legal rights in India under BNS, BNSS, POSH Act 2013, and Domestic Violence Act 2005.

rights.heroSubtitle: Plain-language guide to key laws protecting women in India. General information only, not legal advice.
lawNotes: BNS replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024; BNSS replaced the CrPC and BSA replaced the Evidence Act.
Offences against women and children are grouped in Chapter V of the BNS.
A Zero FIR can be registered at any police station regardless of where the offence happened, and the FIR copy is free.
This is general information, not legal advice. Always verify from official sources.
rights.searchPlaceholder: Search in your language or English (e.g. FIR, 78, workplace)...
rights.noResults: No matching legal entries found. Try another keyword or select All Laws.
rights.entryVerifyNote: Last verified: 2026-11-25 • Verify from official sources.

bns_74.title: Outraging modesty of a woman
bns_74.summary: BNS Section 74 applies when someone assaults or uses criminal force against a woman intending to outrage her modesty, or knowing their act is likely to do so. Offences against women and children are grouped in Chapter V of the BNS (verify exact wording from official sources).
examples: Grabbing, pushing, or touching a woman forcefully in a bus, train, street, or crowded place.
Blocking a woman's path and using unwanted physical force or intimidation.
whatToDo: Move quickly to a lit, populated space and call 112 in immediate danger (or 181 / 1091 for women's support).
Note vehicle numbers, bus/train route, time, place, and witnesses, and file an FIR or Zero FIR at any police station under BNSS Section 173.
bns_74.keyNote: Grouped under Chapter V of the BNS. General information only, not legal advice.

bns_75.title: Sexual harassment
bns_75.summary: BNS Section 75 addresses sexual harassment, including unwelcome physical advances, demands or requests for sexual favours, showing pornography against a woman's will, or making sexually coloured remarks (verify exact statutory text from official sources).
examples: Unwelcome physical contact or explicit sexual remarks in public spaces, hostels, or transit.
Repeated sexual demands or sending explicit material without consent.
whatToDo: Save chats, call logs, messages, or witness names; move away safely and tell a trusted person.
Report via 112 / 181, file an FIR under BNSS Section 173, or if at work, also use the POSH Act 2013 Internal Committee (IC) / SHe-Box portal (verify).
bns_75.keyNote: Applies across public and private settings; workplace cases may also be addressed under POSH Act 2013 (verify).

bns_76.title: Assault with intent to disrobe
bns_76.summary: BNS Section 76 covers assaulting or using criminal force against any woman—or abetting such an act—with the intention of disrobing her or compelling her to be naked (verify exact provisions from official sources).
examples: Pulling, tearing, or forcibly removing a woman's clothing in public or private.
Using physical force or threats to compel someone to undress.
whatToDo: Prioritise immediate physical safety: call 112 first, seek shelter with trusted people or nearby authorities, and get medical attention if injured.
Preserve torn clothing or physical/digital evidence safely and register an FIR or Zero FIR under BNSS Section 173 (the FIR copy is free).
bns_76.keyNote: Serious offence under Chapter V of the BNS. Always seek urgent police/medical help via 112 first.

bns_77.title: Voyeurism
bns_77.summary: BNS Section 77 protects a woman's privacy in private moments. It covers watching or capturing images or videos of a woman engaging in a private act where she expects privacy, or sharing/disseminating such images without her consent (verify from official sources).
examples: Hidden cameras in changing rooms, washrooms, hostels, or hotel rooms.
Recording or sharing private photos or videos without consent—even if someone consented to recording earlier, sharing without consent is covered (verify).
whatToDo: Do not delete messages or links; capture URLs, usernames, dates, and uncropped screenshots safely.
Call 112 if a hidden device is found on-site; report online sharing on cybercrime.gov.in (verify) and file an FIR under BNSS Section 173.
bns_77.keyNote: Covers both physical recording and sharing private imagery without consent (verify exact scope from official sources).

bns_78.title: Stalking
bns_78.summary: BNS Section 78 covers both physical stalking and cyberstalking: following a woman or attempting to contact her repeatedly to foster personal interaction despite a clear indication of disinterest, or monitoring her use of the internet, email, or electronic communication (verify exact provisions).
examples: Repeatedly waiting outside a college, hostel, office, or home, or following someone's commute.
Creating repeated new phone numbers or fake profiles to message after being blocked, or tracking online activity.
whatToDo: Clearly state once (if safe) that you do not want contact, then save call logs, screenshots, dates, and CCTV locations.
Vary your travel route/times, alert trusted contacts, and report via 112 / 181, cybercrime.gov.in (for online stalking; verify), or Zero FIR (BNSS Section 173).
bns_78.keyNote: Covers both offline following and online monitoring (verify exceptions/details from official sources).

bns_79.title: Insulting the modesty of a woman
bns_79.summary: BNS Section 79 covers uttering words, making sounds or gestures, or exhibiting any object intending that it be heard or seen by a woman to insult her modesty, or intruding upon her privacy (verify exact statutory wording).
examples: Catcalling, obscene gestures, lewd comments, or harassing phone calls/voice notes.
Intentionally intruding upon a woman's private space to intimidate or demean her.
whatToDo: Move to a safe, populated place and record time, location, caller numbers, or witnesses.
Call 1091 / 181 (or 112 in immediate danger) and submit a complaint or FIR under BNSS Section 173.
bns_79.keyNote: Applies to verbal, gestural, and privacy-intrusion acts under Chapter V of the BNS.

bnss_173.title: Filing an FIR, including Zero FIR and e-FIR
bnss_173.summary: BNSS Section 173 sets out how information of a cognisable offence is recorded as an FIR. Crucially, you can file a Zero FIR at any police station regardless of where the offence happened, use e-FIR where notified, and receive a copy of the FIR completely free of cost (verify local e-FIR rules).
examples: An incident happened while travelling in another city or district, and you report it at the police station closest to your home or destination.
Submitting an electronic complaint (e-FIR) on an official state police portal where enabled (verify state procedure).
whatToDo: Write down a clear, factual summary (who, what, when, where) and carry two copies so you can ask for a stamped receipt.
If the station says the area is outside their limit, politely request a Zero FIR under BNSS Section 173 and ask for your free FIR copy.
bnss_173.keyNote: BNSS replaced the CrPC on 1 July 2024. The informant is entitled to a free copy of the FIR.

bnss_175_3.title: If police refuse to register an FIR
bnss_175_3.summary: If a police station refuses or delays registering your FIR, the law gives you a clear two-step escalation path: first write to the Superintendent of Police, and if no action follows, approach the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3) (verify exact procedure).
examples: An officer tells you to come back later without recording your complaint, or declines a Zero FIR.
No action is taken even after submitting a written complaint at the station.
whatToDo: Step 1: Send the substance of your complaint in writing (by post or in person with receipt) to the Superintendent of Police.
Step 2: Keep postal/receipt proof; if still unregistered, apply to the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3) (seek qualified legal aid if needed).
bnss_175_3.keyNote: Always keep dated copies and dispatch receipts of every written complaint you submit.

posh_2013.title: Workplace sexual harassment (POSH Act 2013)
posh_2013.summary: The POSH Act 2013 protects women (employees, interns, trainees, visitors, or students in covered workplaces) from workplace sexual harassment through a formal Internal Committee (IC) or Local Committee. Complaints can also go through the SHe-Box portal (verify).
examples: Unwelcome physical contact, sexually coloured remarks, or quid-pro-quo pressure in an office, campus workplace, or work-related travel/online meeting.
Hostile work environment created by repeated inappropriate messages or behaviour from a colleague or senior.
whatToDo: Save work emails, chat screenshots, meeting records, and witness names on a personal device.
File a written complaint with your workplace Internal Committee (IC), check the SHe-Box portal (verify), and report criminal acts under BNS/BNSS if needed.
posh_2013.keyNote: Covers physical offices as well as work-from-home/online work interactions (verify current rules from official sources).

pwdva_2005.title: Domestic violence (Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005)
pwdva_2005.summary: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 provides civil protection, residence rights, and support against physical, emotional, verbal, sexual, or economic abuse inside a domestic relationship (verify from official sources).
examples: Physical harm, repeated verbal humiliation, threats, or forced isolation inside the home.
Economic abuse such as taking away earnings, blocking access to basic household resources, or threatening eviction.
whatToDo: If in immediate physical danger, move to a safe room or neighbour's home and call 112 first.
Reach out to 181 (24x7 women helpline) or NCW domestic violence helpline 7827170170 (verify), save medical/injury records, and seek protection orders (verify).
pwdva_2005.keyNote: Provides civil remedies (such as protection and residence orders) alongside any criminal remedies under BNS (verify from official sources).

firGuide.heading: How to File a Complaint or FIR
firGuide.subtitle: Practical steps for Zero FIR, e-FIR, and escalating a refusal (verify from official sources).

steps.title: 1. Zero FIR at Any Police Station (BNSS Section 173)
steps.body: You do not have to visit the station where the incident happened. Ask the officer to record a Zero FIR and request your free copy.

steps.title: 2. e-FIR & Online Cyber Reporting
steps.body: Where enabled by your state police, an e-FIR can be submitted online (verify local rules). For cyber incidents, also report on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 (verify).

steps.title: 3. Escalation If Police Refuse (BNSS Section 175(3))
steps.body: Send a written summary of your complaint by post or in person to the Superintendent of Police. If still unregistered, apply to the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3).

steps.title: 4. What to Carry & Keep Safely
steps.body: Carry a written timeline (date, time, place, details), ID proof, screenshots/call logs, medical notes if any, and always keep a stamped copy or acknowledgement number.

meta.title: Self-Defence | Shakti Shield
meta.description: Basic escape-first self-defence steps with simple illustrations. Always prioritise escaping and calling for help over confrontation.

defence.heroSubtitle: Simple awareness and escape-first steps to create space and reach safety.
defence.priorityBannerTitle: Core Rule: Escape and Call for Help First
defence.priorityBannerBody: Always prioritise getting away, making loud noise to draw attention, and calling 112 over physical confrontation. Use physical moves only to break free and run to safety.
defence.trainingNote: Note: Seek professional, certified self-defence training for safe hands-on practice. General information only.
defence.techniquesSubtitle: Calm, practical steps focusing on balance, weak grip points, and moving away fast.

stance.title: 1. Safe Stance & Voice Boundary
stance.svgAlt: Illustration showing a balanced open stance with both hands raised calmly in front
stance.goal: Goal: Keep balance, protect your space, and attract nearby witnesses.
steps: 1. Step one foot slightly back with knees relaxed so you stay balanced.
2. Raise both open palms to chest height in front of you to keep distance.
3. Speak loudly and firmly ('Stay back! Help!') while looking for the nearest lit shop, crowd, or exit.

wrist.title: 2. Wrist Grab Release (Thumb Gap)
wrist.svgAlt: Illustration showing rotating a grabbed wrist toward the attacker's thumb gap to break free
wrist.goal: Goal: Break a single-hand wrist grip by moving toward the thumb.
steps: 1. Stay calm and step slightly closer for leverage instead of pulling straight backward.
2. Rotate your grabbed arm toward the gap between the attacker's thumb and fingers (the weakest part of the grip).
3. Pull sharply back toward your own shoulder, then turn immediately and run toward people or call 112.

palm.title: 3. Open Palm Push to Create Space
palm.svgAlt: Illustration showing an open palm forward push to create space for escape
palm.goal: Goal: Push away from a close front approach so you can escape.
steps: 1. Keep fingers slightly curled back so the hard heel of your palm leads forward.
2. Push forcefully straight forward at shoulder or chin height using your body weight.
3. Do not stay to fight—immediately step back, shout for help, and move to a safe public place.

barrier.title: 4. Everyday Barriers & Fast Exit
barrier.svgAlt: Illustration showing holding a bag as a barrier while moving toward an illuminated exit
barrier.goal: Goal: Use a bag or everyday object to keep distance while leaving.
steps: 1. Hold a backpack, handbag, or umbrella between yourself and someone approaching too closely.
2. Drop heavy items if they slow you down while running to safety.
3. Move straight into a busy store, transit station, or lit area and call 112 or 181.

questions.q: You are walking alone at night and notice someone following you persistently. What is the safest first step?
options: Confront them alone in a quiet side street.
Move immediately into a bright shop or busy area and call 112 or a trusted contact.
Put on both earphones and walk faster without looking around.
questions.explanation: Always prioritise moving toward light, people, and safety, and calling 112 over confrontation.

questions.q: An incident happened in another city while you were travelling. Can you file an FIR at your local police station?
options: Yes. Under BNSS Section 173, a Zero FIR can be registered at any police station, and the FIR copy is free.
No. Police can only register an FIR in the city where the incident occurred.
Yes, but only after paying a fee for the FIR copy.
questions.explanation: BNSS Section 173 allows Zero FIR registration at any police station regardless of jurisdiction, and the FIR copy is free.

questions.q: An unknown online account threatens to share edited photos of you unless you send money. What should you do?
options: Pay once quickly so they delete the photos.
Delete the chat immediately without saving anything.
Do not pay; save full screenshots with URLs, block the account, and report on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 (verify).
questions.explanation: Never pay blackmail demands. Save uncropped evidence with URLs and report via cybercrime.gov.in or 1930 (verify).

questions.q: What can you do if a police station refuses to register your FIR?
options: Stop trying because there is no other option.
Write to the Superintendent of Police, then approach the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3).
Wait without keeping any written record of the refusal.
questions.explanation: If police refuse to register an FIR, write to the Superintendent of Police and then approach the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3).

questions.q: You experience repeated unwelcome remarks at your workplace. Where can you seek formal redressal?
options: Through your workplace Internal Committee (IC) under the POSH Act 2013 or via the SHe-Box portal (verify).
Only by posting anonymously on social media.
Nowhere, if the remarks happened on a work chat.
questions.explanation: Workplace sexual harassment is covered under the POSH Act 2013, and complaints can also go through the SHe-Box portal (verify).

questions.q: Before getting into a booked cab or auto at night, what should you check first?
options: Get in quickly without checking the number plate.
Ask the driver to switch off route navigation.
Match the vehicle registration number with the booking app and share trip details with a trusted contact.
questions.explanation: Verifying the vehicle number plate and sharing trip details with a trusted contact helps keep night travel safer.

empowerment.storiesSubtitle: Short factual summaries of publicly documented Indian women across science, sport, and technology.

stories.name: Kalpana Chawla
stories.summary: Born in Karnal, Haryana, Kalpana Chawla earned a degree in aeronautical engineering in India before moving to the United States, where she became the first woman of Indian origin to fly in space aboard Space Shuttle Columbia (1997 and 2003).

stories.name: M. C. Mary Kom
stories.summary: Hailing from Kangathei in Manipur, Mary Kom balanced early training and family responsibilities to win an Olympic bronze medal at London 2012 and become a six-time World Amateur Boxing Champion.

stories.name: Sudha Murty
stories.summary: Born in Shiggaon, Karnataka, Sudha Murty worked as a computer scientist and engineer before leading the Infosys Foundation's education and community initiatives, and received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

careerTips.title: Build a Clear, Evidence-Based CV

careerTips.title: Verify Job Offers & Employers
careerTips.body: Research company websites, official email domains, and never pay security deposits or fees to get an interview.

careerTips.title: Strengthen Digital & Communication Skills
careerTips.body: Practise writing concise emails, speaking clearly about your work, and backing up your portfolio safely.

careerTips.title: Seek Mentors & Peer Networks
careerTips.body: Connect with seniors, faculty, or women's professional groups to learn about verified openings and scholarships.
